authority: Alaska Division of Elections; U.S. Election Assistance Commission; U.S. Census Bureau; Verified Voting

completionDecision.reason: Official Alaska Division of Elections result artifacts and election-applicable boundary plans now support reviewed 2012, 2016, 2020, and 2024 precinct packages. For 2024, 402 geographic precincts have exact reviewed polygons and 121 absentee, early-voting, questioned-ballot, federal-overseas, and administrative units remain explicitly non-geographic. Presidential totals reconcile exactly; the U.S. House named-candidate comparison remains 750 votes below the statewide summary because write-ins are not itemized. The guarded GIS release is locally validated but not production-activated. No precinct or vote is allocated to a borough/census-area FIPS, and cross-election precinct stability is not inferred.

displayCaveats: The guarded four-election precinct packages are locally complete but remain unavailable publicly until the separate production release is activated.
Review rows are official precinct/reporting-unit source-review rows, not proof of fraud or misconduct.
U.S. House comparison rows are ranked-choice first-choice named-candidate rows and omit 750 statewide write-in votes not itemized in the ENR precinct CSV.
Only exact geographic precinct identities join to polygons; absentee, early, question, federal-overseas, remote, and administrative units remain unpainted.
ENR Reg_voters and total_ballots reconcile statewide after de-duplication, but mixed reporting-unit rows are not active turnout denominator rows without source-side semantics.
Wave 2 turnout verification keeps ENR Reg_voters/total_ballots as a documented state-native lead only; active turnout remains the EAC statewide fallback.
Alaska's 30 Census county-equivalent FIPS entries are registry geometry only; neither precincts nor votes are allocated to them.
Each election keeps its own precinct boundary vintage. Cross-year comparison requires a separate reviewed common-geography translation.
